title.zh: 卷一百二十九 載記第二十九 沮渠蒙遜
title.raw: 卷一百二十九 載記第二十九 沮渠蒙遜 Volume 129 Records 29: Juqu Mengxun

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜，臨松盧水胡人也。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun was a man of the Lu-water Hu of Linsong.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun was a Lu-shui Hu from Linsong.

sentences.zh: 其先世為匈奴左沮渠，遂以官為氏焉。

translations.literal: His ancestors for generations had been the Xiongnu's left Juqu, thereupon taking the office as clan.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had held the Xiongnu title of Left Juqu, and the family took that office as its surname.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜博涉群史，頗曉天文，雄傑有英略，滑稽善權變，梁熙、呂光皆奇而憚之，故常遊飲自晦。

translations.literal: Mengxun broadly crossed the many histories, rather understood celestial patterns, was heroic and outstanding with heroic plans, witty and good at power shifts; Liang Xi and Lü Guang both marveled at yet feared him, therefore he often roamed and drank to dim himself.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun read widely in history, knew something of astronomy, was bold and resourceful, and had a ready wit for stratagem; Liang Xi and Lü Guang both admired and feared him, so he often hid his light beneath feasting and drink.

sentences.zh: 會伯父羅仇、麹粥從呂光征河南，光前軍大敗，麹粥言于兄羅仇曰：「主上荒耄驕縱，諸子朋黨相傾，讒人側目。

translations.literal: It happened that paternal uncles Luoqiu and Quzhou followed Lü Guang to campaign south of the River; Guang's vanguard was greatly defeated. Quzhou spoke to elder brother Luoqiu saying: "The lord above is wasteful, aged, arrogant, and unrestrained; the various sons form factions and overturn one another; slanderers watch with sidelong eyes.
translations.idiomatic: When his uncles Luoqiu and Quzhou followed Lü Guang on the southern campaign, Lü Guang's vanguard suffered a crushing defeat. Quzhou said to his brother Luoqiu, "The ruler is senile and willful, his sons tear at one another in factions, and men who whisper slander watch for their chance."

sentences.zh: 今軍敗將死，正是智勇見猜之日，可不懼乎！

translations.literal: Now the army defeated and generals dying is just the day when the wise and brave are suspected—can one not fear!
translations.idiomatic: The army is broken and the generals are dying—this is the very hour when able men are marked for suspicion. Should we not be afraid!"

sentences.zh: 吾兄弟素為所憚，與其經死溝瀆，豈若勒眾向西平，出苕藋，奮臂大呼，涼州不足定也。

translations.literal: We brothers have long been what they fear; rather than hang dead in ditches and gullies, how is it compared to rallying the host toward Xiping, exiting Tiaodiao, raising arms and great shouting—Liangzhou is not enough to settle.
translations.idiomatic: Our brothers have long been objects of fear; better to lead the host west to Xiping, break out through Tiaodiao, and raise a shout with arms flung high than to die like dogs in a ditch—Liangzhou would be ours for the taking."

sentences.zh: 」羅仇曰：「理如汝言，但吾家累世忠孝，為一方所歸，寧人負我，無我負人。

translations.literal: " Luoqiu said: "The principle is as you say, but our house for generations has been loyal and filial, what one quarter turns to; better others betray me than I betray others.
translations.idiomatic: " Luoqiu replied, "Your reasoning is sound, yet our family has been loyal for generations and this region looks to us; I would rather another betray me than betray another."

sentences.zh: 」俄而皆為光所殺。

translations.literal: " Before long both were killed by Guang.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long Lü Guang had them both put to death."

sentences.zh: 宗姻諸部會葬者萬餘人，蒙遜哭謂眾曰：「昔漢祚中微，吾之乃祖翼獎竇融，保寧河右。

translations.literal: Clan and marriage various divisions assembling for the funeral exceeded ten thousand; Mengxun wept and said to the masses: "Formerly when Han's mandate was mid-faint, my great-grandfather aided and encouraged Dou Rong, preserving and quieting the west of the River.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand kinsmen and allies came to the funeral. Mengxun wept and told the crowd, "When the Han mandate faltered, my ancestor aided Dou Rong and helped secure the country west of the Yellow River."

sentences.zh: 呂王昏耄，荒虐無道，豈可不上繼先祖安時之志，使二父有恨黃泉！

translations.literal: The Lü king is dim and aged, wasteful and cruel without the Way—how can we not upward continue the ancestors' intent to pacify the times, causing the two fathers to harbor resentment in the Yellow Springs!
translations.idiomatic: The Lü king is senile and cruel without principle—can we fail to carry on our forebears' wish for peace and leave our two fathers unrevenged in the grave!"

sentences.zh: 」眾咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: " The mass all shouted ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: " The crowd shouted their assent."

sentences.zh: 遂斬光中田護軍馬邃、臨松令井祥以盟，一旬之間，眾至萬餘。

translations.literal: Thereupon they beheaded Guang's central-field guard commander Ma Sui and Linsong magistrate Jing Xiang to covenant; within one ten-day, the host reached over ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They slew Ma Sui, the central-field guard under Lü Guang, and Jing Xiang, magistrate of Linsong, to seal their oath, and within ten days their following passed ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 屯據金山，與從兄男成推光建康太守段業為使持節、大都督、龍驤大將軍、涼州牧、建康公，改呂光龍飛二年為神璽元年。

translations.literal: They encamped and held Jin Mountain; with elder male cousin Nancheng they raised Guang's Jiankang governor Duan Ye as commissioner bearing credentials, grand commander, soaring-dragon great general, Liangzhou shepherd, Duke of Jiankang, changing Lü Guang's second year of Longfei to the first year of Shenxi.
translations.idiomatic: They occupied Jin Mountain and, with his cousin Juqu Nancheng, set up Duan Ye, Lü Guang's governor of Jiankang, as commissioner with full powers, grand commander, grand general soaring dragon, governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Jiankang, reckoning the first year of their rule from Lü Guang's second year of Longfei under the new era name Shenxi.

sentences.zh: 業以蒙遜為張掖太守，男成為輔國將軍，委以軍國之任。

translations.literal: Ye appointed Mengxun as Zhangye governor, Nancheng as bulwark-of-state general, entrusting them army and state's tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye named Mengxun governor of Zhangye and Nancheng general who supports the state, entrusting them with civil and military power.

sentences.zh: 業將使蒙遜攻西郡，眾咸疑之。

translations.literal: Ye was about to order Mengxun to attack Xijun; the mass all doubted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Ye was about to send Mengxun against Xijun, his officers were skeptical.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜曰：「此郡據嶺之要，不可不取。

translations.literal: Mengxun said: "This commandery holds the pass's key; cannot but take it.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun said, "That commandery guards the ridge line; we must take it."

sentences.zh: 」業曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: " Ye said: "Your words are right.
translations.idiomatic: " Duan Ye said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 」遂遣之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon sent him.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent him off."

sentences.zh: 蒙遜引水灌城，城潰，執太守呂純以歸。

translations.literal: Mengxun led water to flood the city; the city collapsed; seized governor Lü Chun and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun broke the dikes and flooded the walls; the city fell, and he brought back the governor Lü Chun as prisoner.

sentences.zh: 於是王德以晉昌，孟敏以敦煌降業。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang De with Jinchang, Meng Min with Dunhuang submitted to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Wang De then surrendered Jinchang and Meng Min surrendered Dunhuang to Duan Ye.

sentences.zh: 業封蒙遜臨池侯。

translations.literal: Ye enfeoffed Mengxun as marquis of Linchi.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye enfeoffed Mengxun as marquis of Linchi.

sentences.zh: 呂弘去張掖，將東走，業議欲擊之。

translations.literal: Lü Hong left Zhangye, about to flee east; Ye deliberated desiring to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Hong quit Zhangye to flee east, Duan Ye's council urged an attack.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜諫曰：「歸師勿遏，窮寇弗追，此兵家之戎也。

translations.literal: Mengxun remonstrated saying: "Returning hosts do not block; exhausted bandits are not pursued—this is the military family's rong.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun remonstrated, "Do not bar a retreating army or press a cornered foe—such is the soldier's rule."

sentences.zh: 不如縱之，以為後圖。

translations.literal: Better to release them, thereby for later planning.
translations.idiomatic: Better to let them go and plan for another day."

sentences.zh: 」業曰：「一日縱敵，悔將無及。

translations.literal: " Ye said: "One day releasing the enemy, regret will not reach.
translations.idiomatic: " Duan Ye replied, "Let the enemy slip once and regret will come too late."

sentences.zh: 」遂率眾追之，為弘所敗。

translations.literal: " Thereupon led the host pursuing him, was defeated by Hong.
translations.idiomatic: " He led the army in pursuit and was routed by Lü Hong."

sentences.zh: 業賴蒙遜而免，歎曰：「孤不能用子房之言，以至於此！

translations.literal: Ye relied on Mengxun to escape, sighed saying: "I alone could not use Zifang's words, thereby reaching to this!
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye owed his escape to Mengxun and sighed, "I would not heed the counsel of a Zhang Liang, and this is the price!"

sentences.zh: 」業築西安城，以其將臧莫孩為太守。

translations.literal: " Ye built Xi'an city, taking his general Zang Mohai as governor.
translations.idiomatic: " He walled Xi'an and named his general Zang Mohai governor."

sentences.zh: 蒙遜曰：「莫孩勇而無謀，知進忘退，所謂為之築塚，非築城也。

translations.literal: Mengxun said: "Mohai is brave but without plans, knows advance forgets retreat—what is called for him building a tomb, not building a city.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun said, "Mohai is brave but witless, ever eager to advance and never to withdraw—you are digging his grave, not raising a wall for him."

sentences.zh: 」業不從。

translations.literal: " Ye did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: " Duan Ye would not listen."

sentences.zh: 俄而為呂纂所敗。

translations.literal: Before long was defeated by Lü Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zang Mohai was defeated by Lü Zuan.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜懼業不能容己，每匿智以避之。

translations.literal: Mengxun feared Ye could not contain himself, always hiding wisdom to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun feared that Duan Ye could not tolerate him and constantly feigned dullness to stay out of his way.

sentences.zh: 業僭稱涼王，以蒙遜為尚書左丞，梁中庸為右丞。

translations.literal: Ye usurpingly styled himself king of Liang, appointed Mengxun as left aide of the masters of writing, Liang Zhongyong as right aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Ye assumed the title of king of Liang, he made Mengxun left secretary of the masters of writing and Liang Zhongyong right secretary.

sentences.zh: 呂光遣其二子紹、纂伐業，業請救于禿髮烏孤，烏孤遣其弟鹿孤及楊軌救業。

translations.literal: Lü Guang dispatched his two sons Shao and Zuan to campaign against Ye; Ye requested rescue from Tufa Wugu; Wugu sent his younger brother Lugu and Yang Gui to rescue Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang sent his sons Shao and Zuan against Duan Ye, who begged aid from Tufa Wugu; Wugu sent his brother Lugu and Yang Gui to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 紹以業等軍盛，欲從三門關挾山而東。

translations.literal: Shao because Ye and others' army was strong, wished to follow Sanmen Pass hugging the mountains eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Shao saw that Duan Ye's host was strong and proposed to slip east along the mountains through Sanmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 纂曰：「挾山示弱，取敗之道，不如結陣衛之，彼必憚我而不戰也。

translations.literal: Zuan said: "Hugging the mountains shows weakness—the way to take defeat; better to array formations and guard them; they will surely fear us and not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan said, "Skirting the mountains advertises weakness and courts defeat; better to form a battle line and hold them—they will fear us and refuse battle."

sentences.zh: 」紹乃引軍而南。

translations.literal: " Shao thereupon led the army southward.
translations.idiomatic: " Lü Shao therefore marched south."

sentences.zh: 業將擊之，蒙遜諫曰：「楊軌恃虜騎之強，有窺覦之志。

translations.literal: Ye was about to strike them; Mengxun remonstrated saying: "Yang Gui relies on barbarian cavalry's strength, has covetous intent.
translations.idiomatic: As Duan Ye prepared to attack, Mengxun remonstrated, "Yang Gui trusts in the strength of his nomad horse and eyes your throne for himself."

sentences.zh: 紹、纂兵在死地，必決戰求生。

translations.literal: Shao and Zuan's troops are on dead ground; they must join battle to seek life.
translations.idiomatic: Shao and Zuan are on deadly ground; they will fight to the death."

sentences.zh: 不戰則有太山之安，戰則有累卵之危。

translations.literal: If not fighting then there is Mount Tai's peace; if fighting then there is piled-eggs' peril.
translations.idiomatic: Refuse battle and you are secure as Mount Tai; join battle and you stand on eggs piled high."

sentences.zh: 」業曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: " Ye said: "Your words are right.
translations.idiomatic: " Duan Ye said, "You speak truly."

sentences.zh: 」乃按兵不戰。

translations.literal: " Thereupon held the army and did not fight.
translations.idiomatic: " He held his troops and gave no battle."

sentences.zh: 紹亦難之，各引兵歸。

translations.literal: Shao also found it hard; each led troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Shao found the situation awkward as well, and both sides withdrew.

sentences.zh: 業憚蒙遜雄武，微欲遠之，乃以蒙遜從叔益生為酒泉太守，蒙遜為臨池太守。

translations.literal: Ye feared Mengxun's heroic martialness, slightly wished to distance him; thereupon made Mengxun's paternal uncle Yisheng Jiuquan governor, Mengxun Linchi governor.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye feared Mengxun's prowess and wished to edge him aside; he named Mengxun's uncle Yisheng governor of Jiuquan and Mengxun governor of Linchi.

sentences.zh: 業門下侍郎馬權雋爽有逸氣，武略過人。

translations.literal: Ye's gatehouse gentleman Ma Quan was handsome and bright with transcendent qi, martial plans surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Quan, a gentleman attendant at Duan Ye's gate, was dashing and brilliant, with military talent above the common run.

sentences.zh: 業以權代蒙遜為張掖太守，甚見親重，每輕陵蒙遜。

translations.literal: Ye used Quan to replace Mengxun as Zhangye governor; he was very seen as intimate and weighty, often lightly insulting Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye replaced Mengxun with Ma Quan as governor of Zhangye and favored him so heavily that Ma Quan regularly slighted Mengxun.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜亦憚而怨之，乃譖之於業曰：「天下不足慮，惟當憂馬權耳。

translations.literal: Mengxun also feared and resented him, thereupon slandered him to Ye saying: "All under Heaven is not worth worry; only ought to worry Ma Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun feared and hated him and said to Duan Ye, "The realm is no concern—only Ma Quan should worry you."

sentences.zh: 」業遂殺之。

translations.literal: " Ye thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Duan Ye had Ma Quan executed."

sentences.zh: 蒙遜謂男成曰：「段業愚暗，非濟亂之才，信讒愛佞，無鑒斷之明。

translations.literal: Mengxun said to Nancheng: "Duan Ye is foolish and dark, not talent to aid disorder, trusts slander and loves flatterers, without mirror-judgment's clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun said to Nancheng, "Duan Ye is a dullard, no man to save a crisis; he heeds slander and dotes on toadies and cannot judge men."

sentences.zh: 所憚惟索嗣、馬權，今皆死矣，蒙遜欲除業以奉兄何如？

translations.literal: What he feared was only Suosi and Ma Quan; now both are dead; Mengxun wishes to remove Ye to serve elder brother—how about it?
translations.idiomatic: He feared only Suosi and Ma Quan, and both are dead. I mean to remove Duan Ye and set you up, brother—what say you?"

sentences.zh: 」男成曰：「業羈旅孤飄，我所建立，有吾兄弟，猶魚之有水，人既親我，背之不祥。

translations.literal: " Nancheng said: "Ye is sojourner alone adrift; what I established; having us brothers is like fish having water; men already are intimate with me; turning the back on them is not auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: " Nancheng replied, "Duan Ye is a wanderer whom we raised to the throne; we are to him as water to fish. The people trust us; to betray him would be ill-omened."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Mengxun dropped the plan."

sentences.zh: 蒙遜既為業所憚，內不自安，請為西安太守。

translations.literal: Mengxun having been feared by Ye, within was not self at peace, requested to be Xi'an governor.
translations.idiomatic: Since Duan Ye still feared him, Mengxun felt uneasy and asked to be governor of Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 業亦以蒙遜有大志，懼為朝夕之變，乃許焉。

translations.literal: Ye also because Mengxun had great aims, feared dawn-and-dusk change, thereupon granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye knew Mengxun nursed a great ambition and feared a coup at any hour, so he granted the request.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜期與男成同祭蘭門山，密遣司馬許咸告業曰：「男成欲謀叛，許以取假日作逆。

translations.literal: Mengxun set a date with Nancheng jointly to sacrifice at Lanmen Mountain, secretly sent major Xu Xian to tell Ye saying: "Nancheng desires to plot rebellion, promising to take a leave day to commit treason.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun arranged to sacrifice with Nancheng on Mount Lanmen while secretly sending his aide Xu Xian to Duan Ye with the report that Nancheng planned revolt and would use a holiday leave to strike."

sentences.zh: 若求祭蘭門山，臣言驗矣。

translations.literal: If he requests to sacrifice at Lanmen Mountain, your subject's words are verified.
translations.idiomatic: If he asks leave to sacrifice on Lanmen Mountain, you will know my words are true."

sentences.zh: 」至期日，果然。

translations.literal: " When the appointed day arrived, it was so.
translations.idiomatic: " When the day came, Nancheng did exactly as foretold."

sentences.zh: 業收男成，令自殺。

translations.literal: Ye seized Nancheng, ordered him to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye seized Nancheng and ordered him to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 男成曰：「蒙遜欲謀叛，先已告臣，臣以兄弟之故，隱忍不言。

translations.literal: Nancheng said: "Mengxun desires to plot rebellion, already beforehand told your subject; your subject because of brothers' relation, bore it in silence and did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Nancheng said, "Mengxun long ago told me of his plot to rebel, but I held my tongue for our brotherhood."

sentences.zh: 以臣今在，恐部人不從，與臣克期祭山，返相誣告。

translations.literal: Because your subject now exists, he fears the division will not follow; with your subject he set a date to sacrifice on the mountain, then turned to slander and report.
translations.idiomatic: While I live his men might not follow him, so he set this mountain rite with me and then denounced me to you."

sentences.zh: 臣若朝死，蒙遜必夕發。

translations.literal: If your subject dies at dawn, Mengxun will surely rise at evening.
translations.idiomatic: Kill me at dawn and he will rebel at dusk."

sentences.zh: 乞詐言臣死，說臣罪惡，蒙遜必作逆，臣投袂討之，事無不捷。

translations.literal: Beg falsely to say your subject dead, declare your subject's crimes and evil; Mengxun will surely commit treason; your subject will cast sleeve and punish him—affairs without not victory.
translations.idiomatic: Feign my execution and publish my crimes; Mengxun will then rise in open revolt, and I can throw off restraint and strike him—not a stroke can fail.

sentences.zh: 」業不從。

translations.literal: " Ye did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: " Duan Ye would not hear it."

sentences.zh: 蒙遜聞男成死，泣告眾曰：「男成忠於段公，枉見屠害，諸君能為報仇乎？

translations.literal: Mengxun heard Nancheng died, weeping told the masses saying: "Nancheng was loyal to Duke Duan, wrongly saw slaughter and harm—gentlemen, can you avenge him?
translations.idiomatic: When Mengxun heard that Nancheng was dead, he wept before the host and said, "Nancheng was loyal to Lord Duan and has been murdered. Will you avenge him?"

sentences.zh: 且州土兵亂，似非業所能濟。

translations.literal: Moreover the province's soil and soldiers in chaos, seems not what Ye is able to aid.
translations.idiomatic: The province is in arms; Duan Ye is no man to set it right."

sentences.zh: 吾所以初奉之者，以之為陳、吳耳，而信讒多忌，枉害忠良，豈可安枕臥觀，使百姓離于塗炭。

translations.literal: The reason I at first served him was taking him for Chen and Wu; yet trusting slander, much jealousy, wrongly harming loyal and good—how can one pillow in peace and lie watching, causing the hundred surnames to suffer mud and charcoal?
translations.idiomatic: I raised him at first thinking him another Chen Sheng or Wu Guang, yet he trusts slander, suspects everyone, and kills the loyal—can we sleep while the people burn?"

sentences.zh: 」男成素有恩信，眾皆憤泣而從之。

translations.literal: " Nancheng always had grace and trust; the mass all angrily wept and followed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Nancheng had long won the men's love; they wept with rage and rallied to Mengxun."

sentences.zh: 比至氐池，眾逾一萬。

translations.literal: By reaching Dichi, the host exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Dichi his following passed ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍臧莫孩率部眾附之，羌胡多起兵回應。

translations.literal: Garrison-general Zang Mohai led division masses to attach to him; Qiang and Hu many raised troops in echoing response.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Mohai, garrison general, brought his command to join him, and Qiang and Hu bands rose everywhere in support.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜壁于侯塢。

translations.literal: Mengxun walled at Houwu.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun fortified Houwu.

sentences.zh: 業先疑其右將軍田昂，幽之於內，至是，謝而赦之，使與武衛梁中庸等攻蒙遜。

translations.literal: Ye earlier suspected his right general Tian Ang, imprisoned him within; reaching this, apologized and pardoned him, ordered him together with martial guard Liang Zhongyong and others to attack Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye had long suspected his general of the right, Tian Ang, and kept him under house arrest; now he apologized, freed him, and sent him with Liang Zhongyong of the martial guard and others against Mengxun.

sentences.zh: 業將王豐孫言于業曰：「西平諸田，世有反者，昂貌恭而心很，志大而情險，不可信也。

translations.literal: Ye's general Wang Fengsun spoke to Ye saying: "Among Xiping's Tian clan, generation after generation has had rebels; Ang's appearance is respectful but his heart is cruel, aims large but disposition perilous—not trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fengsun warned Duan Ye, "The Tian of Xiping have rebelled in every generation; Tian Ang looks humble but his heart is cruel, his ambition large and his temper treacherous—do not trust him."

sentences.zh: 」業曰：「吾疑之久矣，但非昂無可以討蒙遜。

translations.literal: " Ye said: "I have suspected him long; yet except Ang none can be used to punish Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: " Duan Ye said, "I have doubted him long, yet no one but Tian Ang can face Mengxun."

sentences.zh: 」豐孫言既不從，昂至侯塢，率騎五百歸於蒙遜。

translations.literal: " Fengsun's words not followed, when Ang reached Houwu, led five hundred horse and submitted to Mengxun.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye brushed the warning aside; when Tian Ang reached Houwu he brought five hundred horsemen over to Mengxun.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜至張掖，昂兄子承愛斬關內之，業左右皆散。

translations.literal: Mengxun reached Zhangye; Ang's elder brother's son Cheng'ai cut the pass and admitted him; Ye's left and right all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun marched on Zhangye; Cheng'ai, Tian Ang's nephew, cut the gate bars and let him in, and Duan Ye's guards melted away.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜大呼曰：「鎮西何在？

translations.literal: Mengxun great shouted saying: "Where is the General Who Guards the West?
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun shouted, "Where is the general who guards the west?"

sentences.zh: 」軍人曰：「在此。

translations.literal: " Soldiers said: "Here.
translations.idiomatic: " The soldiers said, "Here."

sentences.zh: 」業曰：「孤單飄一己，為貴門所推，可見丐餘命，投身嶺南，庶得東還，與妻子相見。

translations.literal: " Ye said: "I alone drift a single self, pushed by your noble gate; may I beg spare life, cast body south of the ranges, perhaps obtain east return, to meet wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: " Duan Ye said, "I am one man alone, raised by your house; grant me my life and banish me south of the ranges so I may someday return east to my wife and children."

sentences.zh: 」蒙遜遂斬之。

translations.literal: " Mengxun thereupon beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: " Mengxun beheaded him."

sentences.zh: 業，京兆人也。

translations.literal: Ye was a man of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye came from Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 博涉史傳，有尺牘之才，為杜進記室，從征塞表。

translations.literal: Broadly crossed histories and traditions, had letter-writing talent; was for Du Jin secretary, followed campaign beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: He was well read and a skilled writer; he served Du Jin as secretary and campaigned beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 儒素長者，無他權略，威禁不行，群下擅命，尤信卜筮、讖記、巫覡、征祥，故為奸佞所誤。

translations.literal: A Confucian plain elder, without other power stratagem, awe and prohibition not enforced, the host below usurped orders, especially trusted divination, prophecy records, shamans, and omens; therefore was misled by crafty flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: He was a bookish gentleman without political guile; he could not enforce authority and let his subordinates do as they pleased; he doted on diviners, prophecies, shamans, and omens, and so was led astray by villains.

sentences.zh: 隆安五年，梁中庸、房晷、田昂等推蒙遜為使持節、大都督、大將軍、涼州牧、張掖公，赦其境內，改元永安。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Long'an, Liang Zhongyong, Fang Lu, Tian Ang and others raised Mengxun as commissioner bearing credentials, grand commander, great general, Liangzhou shepherd, Duke of Zhangye, amnestied within his borders, changed era to Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Long'an, Liang Zhongyong, Fang Lu, Tian Ang, and others proclaimed Mengxun commissioner with full powers, grand commander, great general, governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Zhangye, granted an amnesty within his domain, and adopted the era name Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 署從兄伏奴為鎮軍將軍、張掖太守、和平侯，弟挐為建忠將軍、都谷侯，田昂為鎮南將軍、西郡太守，臧莫孩為輔國將軍，房晷、梁中庸為左右長史，張騭、謝正禮為左右司馬。

translations.literal: He appointed elder male cousin Funu as garrison-general, Zhangye governor, marquis of Heping; younger brother Nu as establish-fidelity general, marquis of Dugu; Tian Ang as guard-south general, Xijun governor; Zang Mohai as bulwark-of-state general; Fang Lu and Liang Zhongyong as left and right senior clerks; Zhang Zhi and Xie Zhengli as left and right majors.
translations.idiomatic: He named his cousin Funu garrison general, governor of Zhangye, and marquis of Heping; his brother Nu general who establishes loyalty and marquis of Dugu; Tian Ang general who guards the south and governor of Xijun; Zang Mohai general who supports the state; Fang Lu and Liang Zhongyong chief clerks left and right; Zhang Zhi and Xie Zhengli majors of the left and right.

sentences.zh: 擢任賢才，文武咸悅。

translations.literal: Raising and employing worthy talents, civil and military all rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted able men, and both civil and military arms were pleased.

sentences.zh: 時姚興遣將姚碩德攻呂隆于姑臧，蒙遜遣從事中郎李典聘於興，以通和好。

translations.literal: At the time Yao Xing dispatched general Yao Shuode to attack Lü Long at Guzang; Mengxun sent attendant gentleman Li Dian to visit Xing, thereby to open peace and friendship.
translations.idiomatic: While Yao Xing sent Yao Shuode against Lü Long at Guzang, Mengxun sent his staff officer Li Dian to court Yao Xing and open friendly relations.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜以呂隆既降於興，酒泉、涼寧二郡叛降李玄盛，乃遣建忠挐、牧府長史張潛見碩德于姑臧，請軍迎接，率郡人東遷。

translations.literal: Mengxun because Lü Long had already submitted to Xing, Jiuquan and Liangning two commanderies rebelled and submitted to Li Xuansheng, thereupon sent establish-fidelity Nu, shepherd mansion senior clerk Zhang Qian to see Shuode at Guzang, requesting an army to welcome and lead, leading the commandery people east to migrate.
translations.idiomatic: After Lü Long surrendered to Yao Xing, Jiuquan and Liangning went over to Li Xuansheng; Mengxun sent his brother Nu and chief clerk Zhang Qian to Yao Shuode at Guzang to ask for an escort and lead his people eastward.

sentences.zh: 碩德大悅，拜潛張掖太守，挐建康太守。

translations.literal: Shuode greatly pleased, appointed Qian Zhangye governor, Nu Jiankang governor.
translations.idiomatic: Shuode was delighted and named Zhang Qian governor of Zhangye and Nu governor of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 潛勸蒙遜東遷。

translations.literal: Qian urged Mengxun east to migrate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qian urged Mengxun to move east.

sentences.zh: 挐私于蒙遜曰：「呂氏猶存，姑臧未拔，碩德糧竭將遠，不能久也。

translations.literal: Nu privately to Mengxun said: "The Lü clan still exists, Guzang not yet taken; Shuode's grain exhausted will be distant, cannot long endure.
translations.idiomatic: Nu said privately to Mengxun, "The Lü still hold out in Guzang; Shuode's supplies will run out and he will withdraw—he cannot stay long."

sentences.zh: 何故違離桑梓，受制於人！

translations.literal: What reason to violate and leave mulberry and catalpa, receive control from others!
translations.idiomatic: Why leave our native soil to become another man's pawn!"

sentences.zh: 」輔國莫孩曰：「建忠之言是也。

translations.literal: " Bulwark-of-state Mohai said: "Establish-fidelity's words are right.
translations.idiomatic: " Zang Mohai said, "The general who establishes loyalty speaks true."

sentences.zh: 」蒙遜乃斬張潛，因下書曰：「孤以虛薄，猥忝時運。

translations.literal: " Mengxun thereupon beheaded Zhang Qian, then issued a writ saying: "I, by empty shallowness, meanly am favored by the times' movement.
translations.idiomatic: " Mengxun executed Zhang Qian and issued an edict: "I am a man of slight merit unworthily raised by the times."

sentences.zh: 未能弘闡大獻，戡蕩群孽，使桃蟲鼓翼東京，封豕烝涉西裔，戎車屢動，干戈未戢，農失三時之業，百姓戶不粒食。

translations.literal: Unable to enlarge and open great offering, cut down and level the host of evils, causing the peach-worm to beat wings in the eastern capital, the great boar to steam-wade the western marches; war chariots repeatedly move, shields and spears not yet stored; farming loses the three seasons' work, the hundred surnames household by household lack grain food.
translations.idiomatic: I have not crushed the rebels or stopped the peach-borer from flapping its wings in the eastern capital nor the great boar from trampling the western march; chariots roll without cease, arms are never laid down, the seasons' farming is lost, and the people go hungry from door to door."

sentences.zh: 可蠲省百徭，專功南畝，明設科條，務盡地利。」

translations.literal: May remit and cut the hundred corvées, devote effort to the southern acres, clearly set statutes and articles, strive to exhaust earth's profit."
translations.idiomatic: Let corvée be lightened so men may turn to the southern fields; set clear laws and wring the best from the soil."

sentences.zh: 時梁中庸為西郡太守，西奔李玄盛。

translations.literal: At the time Liang Zhongyong was Xijun governor, fled west to Li Xuansheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zhongyong, then governor of Xijun, fled west to Li Xuansheng.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜聞之，笑曰：「吾與中庸義深一體，而不信我，但自負耳，孤豈怪之！

translations.literal: Mengxun heard it, laughed saying: "I and Zhongyong in righteousness are deep as one body, yet he does not trust me—only self-bears blame; how would I alone blame him!
translations.idiomatic: When Mengxun heard the news he laughed and said, "Zhongyong and I were as one in honor; if he could not trust me, the fault is his own—I bear him no grudge!"

sentences.zh: 」乃盡歸其妻孥。

translations.literal: " Thereupon wholly returned his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent back Zhongyong's wife and children untouched."

sentences.zh: 蒙遜下令曰：「養老乞言，晉文納輿人之誦，所以能招禮英奇，致時邕之美。

translations.literal: Mengxun issued order saying: "Nurturing the aged and begging words, Jin Wen accepted the cart-men's chant—thereby able to summon and treat the heroic and strange, bring the age's harmony's beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun issued an order: "When Duke Wen of Jin honored the old and listened to the songs of the cart drivers, he drew worthy men and brought harmony to the age."

sentences.zh: 況孤寡德，智不經遠，而可不思聞讜言以自鏡哉！

translations.literal: Moreover I, orphaned and lacking virtue, wisdom not spanning far—yet how can one not think to hear straight words to mirror self!
translations.idiomatic: How much more I, a man of shallow virtue and no long view—can I refuse to seek honest counsel for a mirror to my rule!

sentences.zh: 內外群僚，其各搜揚賢雋，廣進芻蕘，以匡孤不逮。」

translations.literal: Inner and outer host of officials, each search and raise worthy and outstanding, broadly advance fodder-cutters' plans, thereby to rectify my not reaching."
translations.idiomatic: Let every officer within and without seek out the worthy and bring forward even the humblest counsel, to amend where I fall short."

sentences.zh: 遣輔國臧莫孩襲山北虜，大破之。

translations.literal: He sent bulwark-of-state Zang Mohai to raid the northern tribes beyond the mountains and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zang Mohai to strike the tribes north of the ranges and broke them decisively.

sentences.zh: 姚興遣將齊難率眾四萬迎呂隆，隆勸難伐蒙遜，難從之。

translations.literal: Yao Xing dispatched general Qi Nan leading a host of forty thousand to welcome Lü Long; Long urged Nan to campaign against Mengxun, and Nan followed.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent Qi Nan with forty thousand men to escort Lü Long; Lü Long persuaded Qi Nan to attack Mengxun, and Qi Nan agreed.

sentences.zh: 莫孩敗其前軍，難乃結盟而還。

translations.literal: Mohai defeated his vanguard; Nan then made covenant and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Mohai shattered Qi Nan's van, whereupon Qi Nan made peace and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜伯父中田護軍親信、臨松太守孔篤並驕奢侵害，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: Mengxun's paternal uncles central-field guard intimate Qinxin and Linsong governor Kong Du together were arrogant and wasteful, encroaching and harming; the hundred surnames suffered them.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun's uncles Qinxin, warden of the central fields, and Kong Du, governor of Linsong, were arrogant predators, and the people groaned under them.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜曰：「亂吾國者，二伯父也，何以綱紀百姓乎！

translations.literal: Mengxun said: "Those who disorder my state are the two uncles—how thereby to regulate the hundred surnames!"
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun said, "Those two uncles are the men who ruin my state—how can I rule the people while they live!"

sentences.zh: 」皆令自殺。

translations.literal: He ordered both to kill themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He compelled both to take their own lives.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜襲狄洛磐於番禾，不克，遷其五百餘戶而還。

translations.literal: Mengxun raided Di Luoquan at Fanhe, did not overcome him, moved more than five hundred households and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun struck Di Luoquan at Fanhe, failed to take him, and carried off over five hundred households on the retreat.

sentences.zh: 姚興遣使人梁斐、張構等拜蒙遜鎮西大將軍、沙州刺史、西海侯。

translations.literal: At the time Yao Xing dispatched envoys Liang Fei and Zhang Gou and others to appoint Mengxun general who guards the west, governor of Shazhou, marquis of Xihai.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent Liang Fei and Zhang Gou to invest Mengxun as grand general who guards the west, governor of Shazhou, and marquis of Xihai.

sentences.zh: 時興亦拜禿髮傉檀為車騎將軍，封廣武公。

translations.literal: At the time Xing also appointed Tufa Nutan chariot-and-cavalry general, enfeoffing him duke of Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing at the same time named Tufa Nutan general of chariots and cavalry and duke of Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜聞之，不悅，謂斐等曰：「傉檀上公之位，而身為侯者何也！

translations.literal: Mengxun heard it, was not pleased, said to Fei and others: "Nutan holds upper duke rank, yet his person is marquis—why!"
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun took this ill and asked the envoys, "Nutan enjoys a higher noble rank than I, yet I am only a marquis—how is that fair?"

sentences.zh: 」構對曰：「傉檀輕狡不仁，款誠未著，聖朝所以加其重爵者，褒其歸善即敘之義耳。

translations.literal: Gou replied saying: "Nutan is light, crafty, and not benevolent; sincere good faith not yet manifest—the sagely court therefore added his heavy noble is to praise his returning to good and immediate ordering's meaning only.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gou answered, "Nutan is fickle and cruel and has not proved his loyalty; the court raised his rank only to reward his willingness to submit."

sentences.zh: 將軍忠貫白日，勳高一時，當入諧鼎味，匡贊帝室，安可以不信待也。

translations.literal: The general's loyalty pierces the white sun, merit towers above the age; he ought to enter harmonized tripod flavor, assist and praise the imperial house—how can he be met with distrust!
translations.idiomatic: Your loyalty shines like the sun and your deeds tower above the age; you should soon sit among the highest ministers and aid the throne—how could the court distrust you!"

sentences.zh: 聖朝爵必稱功，官不越德，如尹緯、姚晁佐命初基，齊難、徐洛元勳驍將，並位才二品，爵止侯伯。

translations.literal: The sagely court's nobility must match merit, offices do not surpass virtue—as Yin Wei and Yao Chao aided the mandate at the beginning, Qi Nan and Xu Luo were first-rank fierce generals, yet rank reached only the second grade and noble title stopped at marquis or earl.
translations.idiomatic: In the Later Qin, rank always matches merit—as when Yin Wei and Yao Chao served at the founding, or Qi Nan and Xu Luo led the van—none rose above the second grade and none held more than a marquisate."

sentences.zh: 將軍何以先之乎？

translations.literal: How does the general precede them?
translations.idiomatic: Why should you rank ahead of such men?"

sentences.zh: 竇融殷勤固讓，不欲居舊臣之右，未解將軍忽有此問！

translations.literal: Dou Rong earnestly and firmly declined, not wishing to sit to the right of old ministers—I do not understand the general's suddenly having this question!
translations.idiomatic: Dou Rong modestly refused to outrank the old ministers—why should you take offense at your place in the list!"

sentences.zh: 」蒙遜曰：「朝廷何不即以張掖見封，乃更遠封西海邪？

translations.literal: Mengxun said: "Why does the court not at once enfeoff Zhangye on me, yet instead enfeoff Xihai far away!"
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun said, "Why not enfeoff me at Zhangye outright, instead of pushing me off to distant Xihai!"

sentences.zh: 」構曰：「張掖，規畫之內，將軍已自有之。

translations.literal: Gou said: "Zhangye lies within planned demarcation; the general already possesses it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gou replied, "Zhangye already lies within your grasp."

sentences.zh: 所以遠授西海者，蓋欲廣大將軍之國耳。

translations.literal: The reason for distantly awarding Xihai is surely wishing to enlarge the general's state.
translations.idiomatic: The distant title of Xihai is meant only to widen your domain."

sentences.zh: 」蒙遜大悅，乃受拜。

translations.literal: Mengxun was greatly pleased, thereupon received the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun was satisfied and accepted the investiture.

sentences.zh: 時地震，山崩折木。

translations.literal: At the time there was an earthquake; mountains collapsed and trees broke.
translations.idiomatic: An earthquake struck; mountains slid and timber snapped.

sentences.zh: 太史令劉梁言于蒙遜曰：「辛酉，金也。

translations.literal: Astrologer-in-chief Liu Liang spoke to Mengxun saying: "Xinyou is metal.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liang, director of astrology, told him, "The day xinyou belongs to metal."

sentences.zh: 地動于金，金動刻木，大軍東行無前之征。

translations.literal: Earth moved on metal; metal moved and carved wood—a great army's eastward march is the omen of nothing ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Earthquake on a metal day means metal overcomes wood—an omen that a great host will march east unopposed."

sentences.zh: 」時張掖城每有光色，蒙遜曰：「王氣將成，百戰百勝之象也。

translations.literal: At the time Zhangye city repeatedly had light and color; Mengxun said: "Kingly qi is about to form—an image of a hundred battles, a hundred victories."
translations.idiomatic: A strange glow played over Zhangye; Mengxun said, "The aura of kingship is gathering—an omen of victory in every fight."

sentences.zh: 」遂攻禿髮西郡太守楊統于日勒。

translations.literal: Thereupon he attacked Tufa's Xijun governor Yang Tong at Rile.
translations.idiomatic: He then struck Tufa's governor of Xijun, Yang Tong, at Rile.

sentences.zh: 統降，拜為右長史，寵逾功舊。

translations.literal: Tong submitted; he was appointed right senior clerk, favor surpassing old merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tong surrendered and was named chief clerk on the right with honors above the older retainers.

sentences.zh: 張掖太守句呼勒出奔西涼。

translations.literal: Zhangye governor Gouhule fled out to Western Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Gouhule, governor of Zhangye, fled to the Western Liang.

sentences.zh: 以從弟成都為金山太守，羅仇子也；

translations.literal: He appointed paternal cousin Chengdu as Jinshan governor—son of Luoqiu;
translations.idiomatic: He named his cousin Juqu Chengdu governor of Jinshan—Luoqiu's son;

sentences.zh: 鄯為西郡太守，麹粥子也。

translations.literal: Shan as Xijun governor—son of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Shan governor of Xijun—Quzhou's son.

sentences.zh: 句呼勒自西涼奔還，待之如初。

translations.literal: Gouhule fled back from Western Liang; he treated him as at first.
translations.idiomatic: When Gouhule returned from the Western Liang, Mengxun received him as before.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜率騎二萬東征，次於丹嶺，北虜大人思盤率部落三千降之。

translations.literal: Mengxun led twenty thousand horse east to campaign, halted at Dan Ridge; northern barbarian great man Sinan led three thousand tribes to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun took twenty thousand cavalry east and camped at Danling; the northern chieftain Sinan brought three thousand tents to surrender.

sentences.zh: 時木連理，生於永安，永安令張披上書曰：「異枝同幹，遐方有齊化之應；

translations.literal: At the time linked trees grew at Yong'an; Yong'an magistrate Zhang Pi submitted memorial saying: "Different branches, same trunk—distant regions have the response of equal transformation;
translations.idiomatic: Twin trunks joined in Yong'an; Magistrate Zhang Pi wrote, "Branches from one root show that distant lands are turning to your rule;

sentences.zh: 殊本共心，上下有莫二之固。

translations.literal: different roots, shared heart—above and below have un-second solidity.
translations.idiomatic: separate stocks with one heart show that high and low are bound as one;

sentences.zh: 蓋至道之嘉祥，大同之美征。

translations.literal: this is the utmost Way's auspicious omen, the great concord's fine sign.
translations.idiomatic: this is the great omen of the Way and the sign of universal peace."

sentences.zh: 」蒙遜曰：「此皆二千石令長匪躬濟時所致，豈吾薄德所能感之！」

translations.literal: Mengxun said: "These all are what two-thousand-bushel magistrates and chiefs, not sparing body, aid the times and bring about—how could my slight virtue be able to move them!"
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun said, "That is the work of my magistrates who wear themselves out for the age—not something my meager virtue could conjure!"

sentences.zh: 蒙遜率步騎三萬伐禿髮傉檀，次於西郡。

translations.literal: Mengxun led thirty thousand foot and horse to campaign against Tufa Nutan, halted at Xijun.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun marched on Tufa Nutan at the head of thirty thousand men and halted at Xijun.

sentences.zh: 大風從西北來，氣有五色，俄而晝昏。

translations.literal: A great wind came from the northwest; the qi had five colors; before long daylight went dark.
translations.idiomatic: A gale blew from the northwest in five-colored murk until day turned twilight.

sentences.zh: 至顯美，徙數千戶而還。

translations.literal: Reaching Xianmei, he moved several thousand households and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Xianmei, resettled several thousand households, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 傉檀追及蒙遜於窮泉，蒙遜將擊之。

translations.literal: Nutan caught up to Mengxun at Qiongquan; Mengxun was about to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Nutan overtook Mengxun at Qiongquan; Mengxun prepared to give battle.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「賊已安營，弗可犯也。

translations.literal: The generals all said: "The bandits have already settled camp—cannot be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: His generals said, "The enemy is entrenched—we cannot strike."

sentences.zh: 」蒙遜曰：「傉檀謂吾遠來疲弊，必輕而無備，及其壘壁未成，可以一鼓而滅。

translations.literal: Mengxun said: "Nutan thinks I come from afar weary and worn, surely will be light and without preparation; while his ramparts are not yet finished, can be destroyed with one drum.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun replied, "Nutan thinks us road-weary and will be careless; before his walls are finished one charge will crush him."

sentences.zh: 」進擊，敗之，乘勝至於姑臧，夷夏降者萬數千戶。

translations.literal: He advanced and struck, defeated them, riding victory to Guzang; Yi and Xia who submitted numbered ten thousand and several thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked, routed Nutan, and pressed to Guzang; ten thousand-odd households of Chinese and tribesmen surrendered.

sentences.zh: 傉檀懼，請和，許之而歸。

translations.literal: Nutan feared, requested peace; he granted it and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Nutan sued for peace; Mengxun agreed and marched home.

sentences.zh: 及傉檀南奔樂都，魏安人焦朗據姑臧自立，蒙遜率步騎三萬攻朗，克而宥之。

translations.literal: When Nutan fled south to Ledu, a man of Wei'an, Jiao Lang, seized Guzang and set himself up; Mengxun led thirty thousand foot and horse to attack Lang, overcame him and spared him.
translations.idiomatic: After Nutan withdrew toward Ledu, Jiao Lang of Wei'an held Guzang on his own; Mengxun took thirty thousand men, took the city, and spared Jiao Lang.

sentences.zh: 饗文武將士于謙光殿，班賜金馬有差。

translations.literal: He feasted civil and military officers at the Palace of Humble Light, distributing gold and horses in graded gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted his officers in the Qian'guang Hall and handed out gold and horses by rank.

sentences.zh: 以敦煌張穆博通經史，才藻清贍，擢拜中書侍郎，委以機密之任。

translations.literal: Because Dunhuang's Zhang Mu broadly penetrated the classics and histories, talent and literary polish clear and rich, he raised and appointed him palace secretary gentleman, entrusting him confidential tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mu of Dunhuang, learned and eloquent, was made gentleman of the palace secretariat and entrusted with state secrets.

sentences.zh: 以其弟挐為護羌校尉、秦州刺史，封安平侯，鎮姑臧。

translations.literal: He appointed his younger brother Nu as colonel who protects the Qiang, governor of Qin, marquis of Anping, to garrison Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Nu became colonel of the Qiang, governor of Qin, marquis of Anping, and held Guzang.

sentences.zh: 旬餘而挐死，又以從祖益子為鎮京將軍、護羌校尉、秦州剌史，鎮姑臧。

translations.literal: After ten-odd days Nu died; again he made paternal granduncle Yizi garrison-capital general, colonel who protects the Qiang, governor of Qin (with variant character 剌), to garrison Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Within a fortnight Nu died; Mengxun then named his kinsman Yizi garrison general of the capital, colonel of the Qiang, and governor of Qin to hold Guzang.

sentences.zh: 俄而蒙遜遷于姑臧，以義熙八年僭即河西王位，大赦境內，改元玄始。

translations.literal: Before long Mengxun moved to Guzang; in the eighth year of Yixi he usurpingly assumed the title of king of Hexi, greatly amnestied within his borders, changed era to Xuanshi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Mengxun moved his seat to Guzang; in the eighth year of Yixi he took the title of king of Hexi, proclaimed a general amnesty, and adopted the era name Xuanshi.

sentences.zh: 置官僚，如呂光為三河王故事。

translations.literal: He set up officials and clerks according to the precedent when Lü Guang became king of Sanhe.
translations.idiomatic: He organized a full administration on the model of Lü Guang's enthronement as king of Sanhe.

sentences.zh: 繕宮殿，起城門諸觀。

translations.literal: He repaired palace halls and raised gate towers and belvederes.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the palaces and raised gate towers and viewing pavilions.

sentences.zh: 立其子政德為世子，加鎮衛大將軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: He established his son Zhengde as heir, adding grand general who guards the court and supervisor of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: He named his heir Zhengde and added the titles grand general of the guard and supervisor of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 傉檀來伐，蒙遜敗之於若厚塢。

translations.literal: Nutan came to attack; Mengxun defeated him at Ruohouwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Nutan invaded, Mengxun defeated him at Ruohouwu.

sentences.zh: 傉檀湟河太守文支據湟川，護軍成宜侯率眾降之。

translations.literal: Nutan's Huanghe governor Wen Zhi held the Huangchuan; guard commander Marquis Cheng Yi led the host to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhi, Nutan's governor on the Huang River, held the Huangchuan, while Cheng Yi, guard commander, brought his command over to Mengxun.

sentences.zh: 署文支鎮東大將軍、廣武太守、振武侯，成宜侯為振威將軍、湟川太守，以殿中將軍王建為湟河太守。

translations.literal: He appointed Wen Zhi grand general who guards the east, governor of Guangwu, marquis of Zhenwu; Cheng Yi as general who rouses might, governor of Huangchuan; and palace general Wang Jian as Huanghe governor.
translations.idiomatic: He named Wen Zhi grand general of the east, governor of Guangwu, and marquis of Zhenwu; Cheng Yi general who rouses might and governor of Huangchuan; and Wang Jian of the palace guard as governor of the Huang River.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜下書曰：「古先哲王應期撥亂者，莫不經略八表，然後光闡純風。

translations.literal: Mengxun issued a writ saying: "Ancient sage kings who answered the period and set right disorder, none did not plan the eight outer regions, then afterward brightly open pure wind.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun proclaimed, "The sage kings of old who met their hour and quelled chaos always secured the outer marches before they spread pure rule."

sentences.zh: 孤雖智非靖難，職在濟時，而狡虜傉檀鴟峙舊京，毒加夷夏。

translations.literal: I, although wisdom is not that which quiets disaster, duty lies in aiding the times, yet the crafty captive Nutan owl-perches on the old capital, poison reaching Yi and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am no master of saving the age, it is my charge to aid the times, while that bandit Nutan perches like an owl on the old capital and poisons Chinese and barbarian alike."

sentences.zh: 東苑之戮，酷甚長平，邊城之禍，害深獫狁。

translations.literal: The slaughter in the eastern park was crueler than Changping; the border cities' disaster harmed deeper than the Xianyun.
translations.idiomatic: The massacre in the eastern park outdid Changping; the harm to the frontier ran deeper than the Xianyun raids."

sentences.zh: 每念蒼生之無辜，是以不遑啟處，身疲甲胄，體倦風塵。

translations.literal: Each time I think of the dark people's guiltlessness, therefore I have no leisure to rest; body weary in armor, form tired in wind and dust.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I think of the innocent people, I cannot rest; I wear armor until I drop and ride the dust without pause."

sentences.zh: 雖傾其巢穴，傉檀猶未授首。

translations.literal: Although I have overturned his nest, Nutan still has not offered his head.
translations.idiomatic: Though I have torn up his lair, Nutan still lives.

sentences.zh: 傉檀弟文支追項伯歸漢之義，據彼重籓，請為臣妾。

translations.literal: Nutan's younger brother Wen Zhi, tracing Xiang Bo's meaning in returning to Han, holds that heavy screen and requests to be minister and concubine.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Wen Zhi, like Xiang Bo who went over to Han, holds a key bastion and begs to become my subject."

sentences.zh: 自西平已南，連城繼順。

translations.literal: From Xiping south, linked cities in succession submit.
translations.idiomatic: South of Xiping the walled towns surrender in a chain.

sentences.zh: 惟傉檀窮獸，守死樂都。

translations.literal: Only Nutan, cornered beast, guards death at Ledu.
translations.idiomatic: Only Nutan, a beast at bay, clings to Ledu.

sentences.zh: 四支既落，命豈久全！

translations.literal: The four limbs already fallen—how can life long endure!
translations.idiomatic: With his limbs cut away, how long can he last!"

sentences.zh: 五緯之會已應，清一之期無賒，方散馬金山，黎元永逸。

translations.literal: The five cords' conjunction already responds; the pure-one's term not distant—then I shall loose horses at Jin Mountain and the black-haired people rest forever.
translations.idiomatic: The conjunction of the five planets answers our rise; the day of unification is near—then we shall turn the horses loose at Jinshan and the people know lasting peace."

sentences.zh: 可露布遠近，咸使聞知。」

translations.literal: May a bulletin be spread far and near, all causing to hear and know."
translations.idiomatic: Let this be proclaimed far and wide so every ear may hear."

sentences.zh: 蒙遜西如苕藋，遣冠軍伏恩率騎一萬襲卑和、烏啼二虜，大破之，俘二千餘落而還。

translations.literal: Mengxun went west as far as Tiaodiao, sent champion Fu En leading ten thousand horse to raid the Boho and Wuti two tribes, greatly defeated them, capturing more than two thousand camps and returning.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun rode west to Tiaodiao and sent Fu En with ten thousand cavalry against the Boho and Wuti tribes, shattering them and bringing back over two thousand camps.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜寢於新台，閹人王懷祖擊蒙遜，傷足，其妻孟氏擒斬之，夷其三族。

translations.literal: Mengxun slept on the new terrace; eunuch Wang Huaizu struck Mengxun, wounding his foot; his wife Lady Meng seized and beheaded him, extirpated his three clans.
translations.idiomatic: On the new terrace the eunuch Wang Huaizu struck at Mengxun and wounded his foot; Lady Meng seized the assassin, executed him, and wiped out three generations of his kin.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜母車氏疾篤，蒙遜升南景門，散錢以賜百姓。

translations.literal: Mengxun's mother Lady Che was gravely ill; Mengxun ascended the South View Gate and scattered cash to bestow the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother Lady Che lay dying, Mengxun mounted the South View Gate and scattered coins to the people.

sentences.zh: 下書曰：「孤庶憑宗廟之靈，乾坤之祐，濟否剝之運會，拯遺黎之荼蓼，上望掃清氣穢，下冀保寧家福。

translations.literal: He issued a writ saying: "I hope to rely on the ancestral temple's spirit, Heaven and Earth's blessing, to ford the not-yet-stripped turning, save the surviving black-haired from bitter herbs, above hope to sweep clear foul qi, below hope to protect and quiet household blessing.
translations.idiomatic: He issued an edict: "I trust in the spirits of the altars and the favor of Heaven and earth to cross this evil time and lift the people from their misery, to cleanse the foul air above and bring peace to every home below."

sentences.zh: 而太后不豫，涉歲彌增，將刑獄枉濫，眾有怨乎？

translations.literal: Yet the grand empress dowager is unwell, crossing the year it grows—could it be that punishments and prisons are bent and excessive, the masses harbor resentment?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the queen mother's illness lingers—are judgments unjust or the people nursing grievances?"

sentences.zh: 賦役繁重，時不堪乎？

translations.literal: Are taxes and corvée heavy and pressing, the times unbearable?
translations.idiomatic: Are taxes and labor too heavy for the times to bear?"

sentences.zh: 群望不絜，神所譴乎？

translations.literal: Are the host of hopes impure, what spirits condemn?
translations.idiomatic: Have the spirits turned away because our sacrifices are unclean?"

sentences.zh: 內省諸身，未知罪之攸在。

translations.literal: Inwardly examining all bodies, I do not know where crime lies.
translations.idiomatic: I search my heart and cannot see my fault."

sentences.zh: 可大赦殊死已下。

translations.literal: May there be a great amnesty down to those not guilty of capital crime."
translations.idiomatic: Let there be a sweeping amnesty short of capital crimes."

sentences.zh: 」俄而車氏死。

translations.literal: Before long Lady Che died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lady Che died.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜遣其將運糧於湟河，自率眾攻克乞伏熾磐廣武郡。

translations.literal: Mengxun sent his generals to transport grain to the Huang River; he personally led the host to overcome Qifu Chipan's Guangwu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He sent troops to convoy grain to the Huang River while he himself stormed Qifu Chipan's Guangwu commandery.

sentences.zh: 以運糧不繼，自廣武如湟河，度浩亹。

translations.literal: Because transport grain did not continue, from Guangwu went to the Huang River, crossing Haoqian.
translations.idiomatic: When supplies failed he moved from Guangwu toward the Huang River and crossed Haoqian.

sentences.zh: 熾磐遣將乞伏魋尼寅距蒙遜，蒙遜擊斬之。

translations.literal: Chipan sent general Qifu Kuini Yin to oppose Mengxun; Mengxun struck and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan sent Qifu Kuini Yin to block him; Mengxun attacked and killed him.

sentences.zh: 熾磐又遣將王衡、折斐、麹景等率騎一萬據勒姐嶺，蒙遜且戰且前，大破之，擒折斐等七百餘人，麹景奔還。

translations.literal: Chipan again sent generals Wang Heng, Zhe Fei, Qu Jing and others leading ten thousand horse to hold Lejieling; Mengxun fought while advancing, greatly defeated them, capturing Zhe Fei and more than seven hundred; Qu Jing fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan sent Wang Heng, Zhe Fei, and Qu Jing with ten thousand horse to hold Lejieling; Mengxun fought his way forward, routed them, took Zhe Fei and seven hundred others, while Qu Jing fled.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜以弟漢平為折沖將軍、湟河太守，乃引還。

translations.literal: Mengxun appointed his younger brother Hanping as general who breaks the charge, Huang River governor, then led back.
translations.idiomatic: He named his brother Hanping general who breaks the charge and governor of the Huang River, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 晉益州刺史硃齡石遣使來聘。

translations.literal: Jin's governor of Yi, Zhu Lingshi, dispatched envoys to visit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Lingshi, governor of Yi for the Eastern Jin, sent envoys on a courtesy mission.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜遣舍人黃迅報聘益州，因表曰：「上天降禍，四海分崩，靈耀擁于南裔，蒼生沒於醜虜。

translations.literal: Mengxun sent houseman Huang Xun to return the visit to Yi and submitted a memorial saying: "Heaven above sent disaster; the four seas split apart; the numinous radiance is stalled in the southern marches while the black-haired sink among ugly captives.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun sent Huang Xun to Jin with a memorial: "Heaven has scourged the realm; the empire is broken; the royal sun hangs over the south while the people lie under barbarian hooves."

sentences.zh: 陛下累聖重光，道邁周、漢，純風所被，八表宅心。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, piled sage and repeated light, the Way surpasses Zhou and Han; the pure wind's covering—within the eight extremities all dwell in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, sage upon sage, surpasses Zhou and Han; wherever your virtue reaches, the eight quarters turn their hearts to you."

sentences.zh: 臣雖被髮邊徼，才非時雋，謬為河右遺黎推為盟主。

translations.literal: Your subject, although hair unbound on the border, talent not the age's outstanding, wrongly am by Hexi's surviving people pushed as covenant lord.
translations.idiomatic: I, though a tribesman on the frontier and no genius of the age, have been chosen leader by the people west of the River."

sentences.zh: 臣之先人，世荷恩寵，雖曆夷險，執義不回，傾首陽，乃心王室。

translations.literal: Your subject's ancestors, generation receiving grace and favor, although passing through barbarian peril, held righteousness and did not turn; bowing to the sun, then heart in the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: My forebears received your grace generation after generation; through every trial they kept faith and never turned their faces from the Jin sun."

sentences.zh: 去冬益州刺史硃齡石遣使詣臣，始具朝廷休問。

translations.literal: Last winter Governor of Yi Zhu Lingshi sent an envoy to your subject, beginning fully to convey the court's good rest and inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Last winter Zhu Lingshi's envoy brought me word of the court's health and favor."

sentences.zh: 承車騎將軍劉裕秣馬揮戈，以中原為事，可謂天贊大晉，篤生英輔。

translations.literal: I hear the chariot-and-cavalry general Liu Yu is rubbing horses and wielding spears, taking the central plains as his affair—this can be called Heaven aiding great Jin, richly producing heroic assistant.
translations.idiomatic: I hear Liu Yu, general of chariots and cavalry, is shoeing horses and raising spears for the Central Plain—surely Heaven aids great Jin and has sent a true champion."

sentences.zh: 臣聞少康之興大夏，光武之復漢業，皆奮劍而起，眾無一旅，猶能成配天之功，著《車攻》之詠。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that Shaokang's raising Great Xia, Guangwu's restoring Han enterprise, both grasped sword and rose, the host not one brigade, still were able to complete merit matching Heaven, manifest the ode Chegong's chant.
translations.idiomatic: I recall how Shaokang restored Xia and Guangwu rebuilt Han with a sword in hand and barely a regiment, yet their deeds matched Heaven and were sung in the ode Chegong."

sentences.zh: 陛下據全楚之地，擁荊、揚之銳，而可垂拱晏然，棄二京以資戎虜！

translations.literal: Your Majesty occupies all Chu land, holds Jing and Yang's keen edge—yet can hang sleeves in ease, abandon the two capitals to supply barbarian captives!
translations.idiomatic: You hold all of Chu and the spear-points of Jing and Yang—can you sit idle and yield the two capitals to the nomads!"

sentences.zh: 若六軍北軫，克復有期，臣請率河西戎為晉右翼前驅。」

translations.literal: If the six armies turn north and recovery has a date, your subject begs to lead the Hexi Rong as Jin's right wing and vanguard."
translations.idiomatic: When the six hosts wheel north and a day of reconquest is set, I beg to lead the Rong of the west river as the vanguard on your right wing."

sentences.zh: 熾磐率眾三萬襲湟河，漢平力戰固守，遣司馬隗仁夜出擊熾磐，斬級數百。

translations.literal: Chipan led a host of thirty thousand to raid the Huang River; Hanping fought hard to hold firm, sent major Wei Ren to strike by night against Chipan, beheading several hundred ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan struck the Huang River with thirty thousand men; Hanping held fast and sent Wei Ren by night against Chipan, who lost several hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 熾磐將引退，先遣老弱。

translations.literal: Chipan was about to lead away, first sending old and weak.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan prepared to withdraw, sending out the old and weak first.

sentences.zh: 漢平長史焦昶、將軍段景密信招熾磐，熾磐復進攻漢平。

translations.literal: Hanping's senior clerk Jiao Chang and general Duan Jing secretly by letter summoned Chipan; Chipan again advanced to attack Hanping.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Chang and Duan Jing secretly invited Chipan in; Chipan advanced again against Hanping.

sentences.zh: 漢平納昶、景之說，而縛出降。

translations.literal: Hanping accepted Chang and Jing's persuasion and bound himself to come out and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Hanping listened to Jiao Chang and Duan Jing, bound himself, and came out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 仁勒壯士百餘據南門樓上，三日不下，眾寡不敵，為熾磐所擒。

translations.literal: Ren urged a hundred stalwarts to hold the south gate tower three days without coming down; few could not match many, was seized by Chipan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ren held the south gate tower for three days with a hundred men until, overwhelmed, Chipan took him.

sentences.zh: 熾磐怒，命斬之。

translations.literal: Chipan was angry, ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan in his rage ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 段暉諫曰：「仁臨難履危，奮不顧命，忠也。

translations.literal: Duan Hui remonstrated saying: "Ren faced peril and trod danger, roused without sparing life—loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Hui urged him, "Wei Ren faced death fearlessly—that is loyalty."

sentences.zh: 宜宥之，以厲事君。

translations.literal: Ought to pardon him, thereby to encourage serving the lord."
translations.idiomatic: Spare him to teach others how to serve a lord."

sentences.zh: 」熾磐乃執之而歸。

translations.literal: " Chipan thereupon seized him and took him back.
translations.idiomatic: Chipan seized Wei Ren and carried him off.

sentences.zh: 在熾磐所五年，暉又為之固請，乃得還姑臧。

translations.literal: At Chipan's place five years; Hui again for him firmly requested; then was able to return to Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ren spent five years in Chipan's hands until Duan Hui again pleaded for him and he was allowed to return to Guzang.

sentences.zh: 及至，蒙遜執其手曰：「卿孤之蘇武也！

translations.literal: When he arrived, Mengxun grasped his hand saying: "You are my Su Wu!"
translations.idiomatic: When he came home, Mengxun took his hand and said, "You are my Su Wu!"

sentences.zh: 」以為高昌太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gaochang governor.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun named him governor of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 為政有威惠之稱，然頗以愛財為失。

translations.literal: In governing he had a reputation for awe and grace, yet rather by loving wealth was at fault.
translations.idiomatic: As an administrator he combined firmness with kindness, though he was faulted for greed.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜西祀金山，遣沮渠廣宗率騎一萬襲烏啼虜，大捷而還。

translations.literal: Mengxun sacrificed west at Jin Mountain, sent Juqu Guangzong leading ten thousand horse to raid the Wuti tribe, great victory and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun offered sacrifice west of Jin Mountain and sent Juqu Guangzong with ten thousand cavalry against the Wuti tribes, winning a great victory.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜西至苕藋，遣前將軍沮渠成都將騎五千襲卑和虜，蒙遜率中軍三萬繼之，卑和虜率眾迎降。

translations.literal: Mengxun went west to Tiaodiao, sent vanguard general Juqu Chengdu leading five thousand horse to raid the Bohe tribe; Mengxun led the central army thirty thousand following; the Bohe tribe led the host to meet and submit.
translations.idiomatic: He rode to Tiaodiao and sent Juqu Chengdu with five thousand horse against the Bohe while he followed with thirty thousand from the center; the Bohe came out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 遂循海而西，至鹽池，祀西王母寺。

translations.literal: Thereupon followed the sea westward, reaching Salt Pool, sacrificing at the Queen Mother of the West temple.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed the shore west to the salt lakes and sacrificed at the temple of the Queen Mother of the West.

sentences.zh: 寺中有《玄石神圖》，命其中書侍郎張穆賦焉，銘之於寺前，遂如金山而歸。

translations.literal: In the temple was the "Mysterious Stone Spirit Chart"; he ordered palace secretary Zhang Mu to rhapsodize it, inscribed it before the temple, then went as far as Jin Mountain and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The temple held the sacred chart on the black stone; he had Zhang Mu compose a fu on it, carved the text before the gate, and returned by way of Jin Mountain.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜下書曰：「頃自春炎旱，害及時苗，碧原青野，倏為枯壤。

translations.literal: Mengxun issued a writ saying: "Recently from spring scorching drought has harmed the season's seedlings; jade plain green wilds suddenly became withered soil.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed, "Since spring a killing drought has blasted the young crops and turned green fields to dust."

sentences.zh: 將刑政失中，下有冤獄乎？

translations.literal: Could it be that punishments and government miss the mean, below there are unjust prisons?
translations.idiomatic: Are judgments unjust and innocent men in chains?"

sentences.zh: 役繁賦重，上天所譴乎？

translations.literal: Are corvée heavy and taxes weighty, what Heaven condemns?
translations.idiomatic: Are taxes and labor so heavy that Heaven punishes us?"

sentences.zh: 內省多缺，孤之罪也。

translations.literal: Inward examination finds many lacks—it is I alone who am guilty.
translations.idiomatic: The fault is mine alone."

sentences.zh: 《書》不雲乎：'百姓有過，罪予一人。

translations.literal: Does not the Document say: 'When the hundred surnames have fault, the crime is on me alone.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, 'If the people err, the blame is mine.'"

sentences.zh: '可大赦殊死已下。

translations.literal: May there be a great amnesty down to those not guilty of capital crime.
translations.idiomatic: Grant a broad amnesty short of capital crimes."

sentences.zh: 」翌日而澍雨大降。

translations.literal: The next day soaking rain fell greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The next day a soaking rain fell.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜聞劉裕滅姚泓，怒甚。

translations.literal: Mengxun heard Liu Yu had extinguished Yao Hong, was very angry.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Liu Yu had destroyed Yao Hong, Mengxun flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 門下校郎劉祥言事于蒙遜，蒙遜曰：「汝聞劉裕入關，敢研研然也！

translations.literal: Gatehouse collating officer Liu Xiang spoke on affairs to Mengxun; Mengxun said: "You heard Liu Yu enter the passes, dare to be so pleased with yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang offered advice; Mengxun snarled, "You heard that Liu Yu had entered the passes and grew insolent!"

sentences.zh: 」遂殺之。

translations.literal: Thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He had Liu Xiang killed.

sentences.zh: 其峻暴如是。

translations.literal: His severity and violence were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his harsh and violent temper.

sentences.zh: 顧謂左右曰：「古之行師，不犯歲鎮所在。

translations.literal: He turned and said to left and right: "Of old when marching armies, one did not offend against the year star and the garrison star's seat.
translations.idiomatic: He told his attendants, "The ancients never campaigned against the station of the year star and the garrison planet."

sentences.zh: 姚氏舜後，軒轅之苗裔也。

translations.literal: The Yao house is Shun's posterity, Xuanyuan's descendants.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao clan are Shun's line and the blood of the Yellow Thearch."

sentences.zh: 今鎮星在軒轅，而裕滅之，亦不能久守關中。」

translations.literal: Now the garrison star is in Xuanyuan, yet Yu destroyed them—also cannot long hold Guanzhong."
translations.idiomatic: The garrison star now stands in the Scales, yet Liu Yu has destroyed Qin—he too will not long hold the Guanzhong."

sentences.zh: 蒙遜為李士業敗于解支澗，復收散卒欲戰。

translations.literal: Mengxun was by Li Shiye defeated at Jiezhi Stream, again gathered scattered soldiers desiring to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun was routed by Li Shiye at Jiezhi Creek and tried to rally his broken troops for another round.

sentences.zh: 前將軍成都諫曰：「臣聞高祖有彭城之敗，終成大漢，宜旋師以為後圖。

translations.literal: Vanguard general Chengdu remonstrated saying: "Your subject has heard the High Ancestor had Pengcheng's defeat, yet in the end completed great Han—fit to turn the army for later planning.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Chengdu urged him, "Even the Han founder lost at Pengcheng yet built the dynasty—you should withdraw and plan again."

sentences.zh: 」蒙遜從之，城建康而歸。

translations.literal: Mengxun followed it, encamped at Jiankang commandery and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun agreed, drew back to Jiankang commandery in Hexi, and marched home.

sentences.zh: 其群下上書曰：「設官分職，所以經國濟時；

translations.literal: Their host of subordinates submitted memorial saying: "Setting offices and dividing duties is the means to order the state and aid the times;
translations.idiomatic: His officers wrote, "Offices exist to govern the state and meet the hour;

sentences.zh: 恪動官次，所以緝熙庶政。

translations.literal: respectfully moving official order is the means to brighten the myriad tasks.
translations.idiomatic: orderly ranks keep every task in hand;

sentences.zh: 當官者以匪躬為務，受任者以忘身為效。

translations.literal: Those who hold office take not sparing body as task; those who receive charge take forgetting self as effect.
translations.idiomatic: ministers should give their bodies to duty and forget themselves in service."

sentences.zh: 自皇綱初震，戎馬生郊，公私草創，未遑舊式。

translations.literal: Since the royal net first quaked, war horses were born in the suburbs, public and private in rough founding, not yet leisure for old pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Since the dynasty shook, armies have tramped the borders, government was thrown together, and old regulations were neglected."

sentences.zh: 而朝士多違憲制，不遵典章；

translations.literal: Yet court gentlemen mostly violate the statutes and do not follow canons and rules;
translations.idiomatic: Many officials flout the code;

sentences.zh: 或公文御案，在家臥署；

translations.literal: some with official documents on the imperial desk, sign from home lying down;
translations.idiomatic: some sign papers from their beds at home;

sentences.zh: 或事無可否，望空而過。

translations.literal: some affairs neither yea nor nay, pass empty and gone.
translations.idiomatic: some let business pass unanswered."

sentences.zh: 至今黜陟絕於皇朝，駁議寢於聖世，清濁共流，能否相雜，人無勸競之心，苟為度日之事。

translations.literal: Down to now demotion and promotion are cut off from the imperial court, refutation and deliberation sleep in this sage age—clear and muddy flow together, able and unable mix; men lack mind to strive and compete, merely pass the days.
translations.idiomatic: Promotions and reviews no longer reach the throne; the worthy and the base are jumbled together and no one strives—only marking time."

sentences.zh: 豈憂公忘私，奉上之道也！

translations.literal: How is this the way of worrying for the state, forgetting self, serving what is above!
translations.idiomatic: That is no way to serve the state or the throne!"

sentences.zh: 今皇化曰隆，遐邇寧泰，宜肅振綱維，申修舊則。

translations.literal: Now royal transformation daily rises, far and near quiet and peaceful—fit to sternly shake the net's cords, declare and repair old rules.
translations.idiomatic: Now your virtue grows daily and the realm is calmer—it is time to tighten discipline and restore the old rules."

sentences.zh: 」蒙遜納之，命征南姚艾、尚書左丞房晷撰朝堂制。

translations.literal: Mengxun accepted it, ordered south-conquest Yao Ai and masters of writing left aide Fang Lu to compose court-hall regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun agreed and told Yao Ai and Fang Lu to draft regulations for the court hall."

sentences.zh: 行之旬日，百僚振肅。

translations.literal: Put in practice ten days; the hundred officials shook and were solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days every office stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 太史令張衍言于蒙遜曰：「今歲臨澤城西當有破兵。

translations.literal: Astrologer-in-chief Zhang Yan spoke to Mengxun saying: "This year west of Linze city ought to have defeated troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan, director of astrology, said, "This year an army will be broken west of Linze."

sentences.zh: 」蒙遜乃遣其世子政德屯兵若厚塢。

translations.literal: Mengxun thereupon sent his heir Zhengde to encamp troops at Ruohouwu.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun therefore stationed his heir Zhengde at Ruohouwu.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜西至白岸，謂張衍曰：「吾今年當有所定，但太歲在申，月又建申，未可西行。

translations.literal: Mengxun went west to Bai'an, said to Zhang Yan: "This year I ought to settle something, but Grand Year is in shen and the month is also founded shen—not yet able to go west.
translations.idiomatic: At Bai'an he told Zhang Yan, "I should win a field this year, yet the Grand Year and the month both stand in shen—I must not march west."

sentences.zh: 且當南巡，要其歸會，主而勿客，以順天心。

translations.literal: For the nonce ought to tour south, await their returning conjunction, be host and not guest, thereby to follow Heaven's heart.
translations.idiomatic: I shall tour south instead, wait for the enemy to gather, keep the initiative, and follow Heaven's intent."

sentences.zh: 計在臨機，慎勿露也。

translations.literal: The plan lies in adapting to the moment—careful not to reveal it.
translations.idiomatic: Tell no one; we shall decide as events unfold."

sentences.zh: 」遂攻浩亹，而蛇盤於帳前。

translations.literal: Thereupon attacked Haoqian, while a snake coiled before the tent.
translations.idiomatic: He struck at Haoqian, and a serpent coiled before his tent.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜笑曰：「前一為騰蛇，今盤在吾帳，天意欲吾回師先定酒泉。

translations.literal: Mengxun laughed saying: "The former one was soaring snake; now it coils in my tent—Heaven's intent wishes me to turn the army and first settle Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: He laughed and said, "First came the omen of the soaring serpent; now it coils in my tent—Heaven orders me to wheel about and take Jiuquan first."

sentences.zh: 」燒攻具而還，次於川岩。

translations.literal: He burned siege engines and returned, halted at Chuanyan.
translations.idiomatic: He burned his siege train, fell back, and camped at Chuanyan.

sentences.zh: 聞李士業徵兵欲攻張掖，蒙遜曰：「入吾計矣。

translations.literal: He heard Li Shiye was levying troops intending to attack Zhangye; Mengxun said: "He has entered my plan.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Li Shiye was raising an army for Zhangye, he said, "He has walked into my trap."

sentences.zh: 但恐聞吾回軍，不敢前也。

translations.literal: Only I fear hearing my returning army, he will not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: I only fear he will hang back if he hears I have turned back."

sentences.zh: 兵事尚權。

translations.literal: Military affairs esteem shifting advantage.
translations.idiomatic: War turns on deception."

sentences.zh: 」乃露布西境，稱得浩亹，將進軍黃穀。

translations.literal: Thereupon spread bulletin on the western marches, claiming to have taken Haoqian and intending to advance to Huanggu.
translations.idiomatic: He published word along the frontier that he had seized Haoqian and would push on to Huanggu."

sentences.zh: 士業聞而大悅，進入都瀆澗。

translations.literal: Shiye heard and was greatly pleased, advanced and entered Dudujian.
translations.idiomatic: Shiye rejoiced, marched into Dudujian,

sentences.zh: 蒙遜潛軍逆之，敗士業於壞城，遂進克酒泉。

translations.literal: Mengxun secretly moved troops to intercept him, defeated Shiye at Huai city, thereupon advanced and took Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: while Mengxun stole up, broke him at Huai city, and stormed Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 百姓安堵如故，軍無私焉。

translations.literal: The hundred surnames were settled and blocked as before; the army took nothing private.
translations.idiomatic: The people were left undisturbed and the troops took no private plunder.

sentences.zh: 以子茂虔為酒泉太守，士業舊臣皆隨才擢敘。

translations.literal: He appointed his son Maoqian as Jiuquan governor; Shiye's old ministers each were raised according to talent.
translations.idiomatic: He named his son Maoqian governor of Jiuquan and employed Shiye's former officers by their abilities.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜以安帝隆安五年自稱州牧，義熙八年僭立，後八年而宋氏受禪，以元嘉十年死，時年六十六，在偽位三十三年。

translations.literal: Mengxun in Emperor An's fifth year of Long'an styled himself shepherd of the province; in the eighth year of Yixi he usurped the throne; after eight years the Song house received the abdication; in the tenth year of Yuanjia he died, at the time age sixty-six, on the false throne thirty-three years.
translations.idiomatic: He first called himself governor of the province in the fifth year of Long'an under Emperor An, seized the royal title in the eighth year of Yixi, saw the Song accept the abdication eight years later, and died in the tenth year of Yuanjia at sixty-six, having reigned thirty-three years in all.

sentences.zh: 子茂虔立，六年，為魏所擒，合三十九載而滅。

translations.literal: Son Maoqian succeeded; in the sixth year was seized by Wei—together thirty-nine years then extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: His son Maoqian ruled six years before Wei captured him; thirty-nine years in all from rise to fall.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：蒙遜出自夷陬，擅雄邊塞。

translations.literal: The historian says: Mengxun came from barbarian borderlands, monopolized might on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: Mengxun rose from the tribal marches and seized power beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 屬呂光之悖德，深懷仇粥之冤；

translations.literal: Meeting Lü Guang's contrary virtue, he deeply cherished the wrong done Quzhou;
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Guang turned cruel, he avenged the murder of Quzhou;

sentences.zh: 推段業以濟時，假以陳、吳之事。

translations.literal: He raised Duan Ye to aid the times, borrowing the deeds of Chen Sheng and Wu Guang.
translations.idiomatic: he raised Duan Ye as a banner for the hour, as Chen Sheng and Wu Guang once did;

sentences.zh: 稱兵白澗，南涼請和；

translations.literal: He called arms at Baijian; Southern Liang requested peace;
translations.idiomatic: he mustered troops at Baijian and forced Southern Liang to sue for peace;

sentences.zh: 出師丹嶺，北寇賓服。

translations.literal: He sent out the army at Danling; northern raiders submitted as guests.
translations.idiomatic: he marched from Danling and brought the northern tribes to heel.

sentences.zh: 然而見利忘義，苞禍滅親，雖能制命一隅，抑亦備諸凶德者矣。

translations.literal: Yet seeing profit he forgot righteousness, harbored disaster and destroyed kin—although able to command fate in one corner, still he may be counted among those stocked with every vicious trait.
translations.idiomatic: He forgot duty for gain, harbored treachery, and slew his own kin; master of a corner though he was, he ranks among the vicious.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：光猜人傑，業忌時賢。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Guang suspected the heroic; Ye envied the worthy of the hour.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium runs: Lü Guang feared great men; Duan Ye resented talent;

sentences.zh: 游飲自晦，匿智圖全。

translations.literal: Roaming and drinking to dim himself, he hid wisdom to seek survival.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun feasted and played the fool while plotting his survival;

sentences.zh: 凶心既逞，偽績攸宣。

translations.literal: Once his cruel heart had its way, his usurped deeds were proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: when his cruel heart had its way, his usurpation showed plain;

sentences.zh: 挺茲奸數，馳競當年。

translations.literal: He bore such craft and cunning, racing for power in his day.
translations.idiomatic: such cunning drove him to scramble for power in his time.
